title: Shielding interpretation
hints: Think about incomplete shielding within the same shell.
Compare the result with each choice and check its sign, units, or underlying rule.
solution: Protons are added as valence electrons enter the same shell and shield incompletely.
statement:
Why does the effective valence nuclear charge generally increase across Period 3?

[_]{a}

choices: Proton count rises, while same-shell electrons shield incompletely.
Each added electron shields exactly one added proton.
The core gains an entire shell at every step.
Protons are lost while electrons remain fixed.
explanations: The added nuclear attraction is only partly offset.
That would keep effective nuclear charge roughly fixed.
The core is approximately unchanged across the period.
Atomic number rises across the period.
